short: Two wars and a financial collapse, from an election decided by 537 votes.
full:
Bush reached the White House after a five-week recount in Florida that the Supreme Court halted, leaving him the winner there by 537 votes and the loser of the national popular vote. Eight months later the attacks of 11 September 2001 reoriented his presidency entirely.

He invaded Afghanistan in October 2001, created the Department of Homeland Security, and pushed through the Patriot Act. The invasion of Iraq in March 2003 was justified by weapons of mass destruction that were never found; the occupation cost some 4,500 American lives and a far greater number of Iraqi ones, and a troop surge in 2007 was needed to contain the insurgency. Tax cuts in 2001 and 2003 turned surpluses into deficits. The federal response to Hurricane Katrina in 2005 damaged him badly, and he left office in the worst financial crisis since the 1930s.
